# LegatorOCR v0.2.0-pre.11 (pre-release)

Changes since pre.10. Command-line; the window gains only a portable mode.

**Signing**
- `--sign-pdf ... --sign-timestamp --tsa-url URL`: an RFC 3161 time stamp inside the signature (PAdES-B-T). `--verify-pdf-signatures` now reads it back: the time, that it is for exactly this signature, and (with `--tsa-ca`) the authority's signature. Tried against a local OpenSSL authority only, not a public one. No LTV (no OCSP / CRL data).
- The space reserved for a signature grew to 20,000 bytes, so signed PDFs are about 40 KB larger.

**Checks**
- `--verify-document` also reports round outlines (stamps, seals) by shape. Weak hint: on the 12 real pages one of 12 untouched pages was flagged, and 24 of 48 synthetic ring stamps drawn on them were found. No real stamped scan was available.

**Reproducible bytes and portable use**
- With `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` set, the same inputs and options give identical PDF bytes (now a test).
- Portable mode: a `portable.txt` next to the programs keeps GUI settings in `Data`. The Windows release job also builds a PortableApps-layout zip (no launcher `.exe`, icons or installer; never run on a Windows PC).

**Tested and not shipped** (numbers in ROADMAP.md): JPEG-ghost test for double-saved JPEGs (42 % false alarms on a held-out set), DjVu shared symbol dictionary (+0.1 to +0.2 % size) and thumbnails (+12.5 %).

Not solved: no hand-verified reference text; no real stamped scans; Windows/macOS builds are CI-only; package recipes unsubmitted; FADGI tables and a public TSA contract are open.
